name: Jahresring
prior: Frippertronics/Eno loops as products are many: Enso Looper (AUv3 iOS/macOS, 'Frippertronics-style dual tape deck' overdub mode, independent speed/direction for record and play; VS: apps.apple.com/app/id1449640589); Qu-Bit Stardust 'cosmic tape looper' (Eurorack, speed shifts pitch, deliberately clean vs. tape's per-pass loss; VS: soundonsound.com/reviews/qu-bit-stardust); jroo loop 'Frippertronics Looper' (Eurorack, varispeed looping delay; VS: perfectcircuit.com/jroo-loop.html); Passepartout Varispeed Looper and Delay (digital tape with degradation when slowed; VS: passepartoutduo.com/varispeed-looper-and-delay); AudioThing/Hainbach Wires (wire recorder with echo, feedback, wow, drops, tilt EQ; VS: cdm.link wires-from-hainbach-audiothing); Chase Bliss Generation Loss MkII (tape degradation effect; VS: chasebliss.com quick guide). Valhalla's history of Eno/Fripp/Riley/Oliveros tape loops (VS: valhalladsp.com/2010/05/26). Myzel already has an Echo return with feedback per bus (APP 1888, 2894) and Körner 'echo (letzte 8 s)' as a live texture source (APP 1722, 4743). Novel pieces here are small: loop length on the Puls bar, tilt = varispeed, shake = erase, and per-ring loss - all of which Enso/Stardust-class tools offer as knobs.
costNotes: Per voice: organ PeriodicWave osc + 2 gains + pan ~0.15-0.2. Per bus (shared, once): DelayNode 16 s stereo + lowpass + WaveShaper('none') + 3 gains + noise + wow LFO ~0.4 (R: section 4 node costs); the feedback cycle is legal because the DelayNode is in it (128-frame minimum, R: section 7). Memory: 16 s x 48 kHz x 2 ch x 4 B = 6.1 MB per bus delay line (A: Blink allocates maxDelayTime up front), 3 buses 18 MB - acceptable. Budget accounting is the real problem: Q.cost is per voice and per engine key; the shared loop needs a phantom-voice surcharge when the first jhr voice starts (as the idea says), which the budget code has no concept of. 2x oversampling on the shaper at L3 adds reported latency inside the loop (R: section 7, WaveShaper latency with oversampling) that would detune the bar-locked loop length - omit. Varispeed by ramping delayTime pitch-shifts correctly (Doppler) but changes the loop period away from the bar.
soundHeld: The voice itself is a plain organ tone at 'direkt' 0.25 - nothing happens for one loop length (2 bars = 4 s at 120 bpm), then the generations arrive. As a sound source this breaks the touch contract: Höhe only sets the tape drive for future rings, setF glides the organ, and Bebung only affects what is being written. Musically the slow accumulation (tanh at 0.3-2.5, lowpass 6 kHz, feedback 0.82: each ring -1.7 dB and darker, noise floor settles at 0.002/(1-0.82) = 0.011 = -39 dB, A) is lovely and exactly Eno/Fripp, but it is the bus effect that is lovely, not the Quelle; a Nebel or Saite into the same loop would be better than the organ. Tempo changes retune every ring (delayTime ramp = Doppler on the whole loop) - must be a fixed-length-in-seconds loop by default, with bar lock as an option. Shake-to-erase works (feedback to 0 for 1 s).
soundBurst: This is where it is musical: Puls blips written into a bar-locked loop return exactly on the beat with decay and darkening = a self-building rhythm (the Riley/Oliveros tape-delay system) and nobody else in Myzel does that. But it is identical to running any struck engine through the Echo return with time = 1 bar and feedback 0.82 plus a lowpass in the return - which the mixer could offer today with two extra controls (tempo-locked time, 'Band' saturation/loss in the return). Failure: four lanes on jhr all write into one shared loop per bus; one lane's loop cannot be shorter than another's.
failureModes: It is an effect: the Quelle (organ) is trivial and the identity lives on the bus; a held note is a 4 s wait
Budget: Q.cost is per voice; a shared per-bus loop has no slot in the accounting (phantom voice hack needed)
Tempo change = Doppler on the whole loop; default to seconds, bar-lock optional
Varispeed by tilt detunes the loop length from the bar for good (the ring stays shifted after the tilt), so bar-lock and tilt exclude each other
Shared loop per bus: Ebene 2 and Puls lanes on the same bus write into the same tape; no per-lane loops
L3 2x oversampled shaper adds latency inside the cycle and detunes the bar lock; omit
Overlaps Echo return (dly) and Körner 'echo (letzte 8 s)'; three tape-ish paths in one app
Bebung/Höhe act only on what is written, not on what is heard; breaks the 'finger shapes the sound' contract
verdict: Common: Frippertronics with varispeed, overdub decks and per-pass degradation exists as Enso (AUv3), Qu-Bit Stardust, jroo loop, Passepartout and Wires; bar lock, tilt varispeed and shake erase are knobs, not a new instrument. Native and cheap (voice ~0.2, loop ~0.4 per bus) but the budget model has no per-bus slot and the 16 s stereo lines cost 6 MB each. As a Klangquelle it fails the contract: the organ is trivial, a held note does nothing for one loop length, Höhe and Bebung only shape future rings. Where it shines - Puls blips returning on the beat, darker each round - is exactly what the existing Echo return would do with a tempo-locked time and a 'Band' loss/saturation stage, and that is the recommendation: deepen Echo (or Körner-echo) instead of building Jahresring, as the idea itself concedes.
